title: Copilot Studio: share autonomous agents with end users (run-only)
summary: Hold: the data-policy command creates a policy but does not configure the connector block advertised in the table, and the sharing-limits command includes explanatory text inside the executable call. The credential-control path also omits the mandatory environment-group route, while the risk rationale treats unconfirmed control coverage as a confirmed exclusion.

claims.where: title; front matter: products; What's changing
claims.claim: This roadmap item concerns Microsoft Copilot Studio run-only sharing of autonomous agents with end users.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot Studio: Share Autonomous Agents to End Users (Run-Only)

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability and Preview release phases.
claims.quote:
"releasePhase": [
    "General Availability",
    "Preview"
  ]

claims.quote: "previewDate": "August CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Scope

claims.quote: "targetDate": "January CY2027"

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap platform is Web.
The roadmap says autonomous agents previously could only be used and managed by makers.
claims.quote: Previously, autonomous agents could only be used and managed by makers, limiting their reach to the people who needed them.

claims.claim: Run-only sharing reaches end users without requiring edit permissions or ownership.
claims.quote: Run-only sharing enables makers to securely share autonomous agents with end users, allowing users to benefit from agent-driven automation without requiring edit permissions or ownership.

claims.where: What's changing; Cost and licensing; Scope; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: A shared autonomous agent must be published with triggers, to Teams + Microsoft 365 with Make agent available in Microsoft Copilot turned on.
claims.quote: Agents you want to share are published to **Teams + Microsoft 365**, with **Make agent available in Microsoft Copilot** turned on.

claims.claim: Makers can give individual users or security groups Can use access.
claims.quote: Enter the user name, email addresses of individual users, or security groups you want to share the agent with. Ensure **Can use** appears beside the search bar.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Security & identity; Scope
claims.claim: Shared autonomous agents run with recipients' own credentials, with triggers and tools configured for user authentication.
claims.quote: You can share a published agent that has triggers with users who need to run the agent by using their own credentials. Before sharing, configure the agent's triggers and tools for user authentication.

claims.claim: Recipients activate the shared agent for themselves through the supplied link.
claims.quote: Recipients can use the *can use* link to activate the agent for themselves, connect the agent with their own credentials, and manage their permitted trigger settings.

claims.where: controls[6].ui; What's changing; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The maker path to run-only sharing is Agents > agent > Share > Can use.
claims.quote: Open the agent from the **Agents** page. ... Select the **Share** ... Ensure **Can use** appears beside the search bar.

claims.claim: Recipients do not receive a notification when the maker shares an autonomous agent.
claims.quote: Sharing visibility: Users don't receive a notification when a maker shares an agent with them.

claims.where: What's changing; Change & support; controls[6].note; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Makers must copy and send the Copy link to set up link to recipients.
claims.quote:
Select **Copy sharing link**, then **Copy link to set up**.
6. Send the link to the end users you shared the autonomous agent with.

claims.claim: The agent cannot run for a recipient until every trigger, tool and workflow requiring their credentials is connected.
claims.quote: An autonomous agent can't run until you connect every trigger, tool, and workflow that requires your credentials.

claims.claim: Recipients can change only trigger options the maker permits through Editable by user.
claims.quote: If you're sharing this agent with others to use, choose which options users can or can't configure themselves by turning on or off **Editable by user** for each option.

claims.claim: Recipients cannot change instructions, tools or other authoring settings.
claims.quote: You can't change the agent's instructions, tools, or other authoring settings.

claims.claim: Users of shared autonomous agents cannot specify or modify tool parameters.
claims.quote: Users of a shared autonomous agent can't specify or modify tool parameters.

claims.claim: Tool calls are invoked and executed fully with AI based on the maker's specifications.
claims.quote: Tool calls are invoked and executed fully with AI, based on the maker's specifications.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: A workflow used as a tool in a shared autonomous agent can accept only end-user credentials.
claims.quote: If your agent calls a workflow as a tool, that workflow can only accept end user credentials for authentication. Workflows that use any maker-only credentials aren't supported for autonomous agents.

claims.claim: Learn documents run-only sharing as preview and the setup and trigger articles are prerelease documentation.
claims.quote:
# Add triggers to an agent (Microsoft Copilot) (preview)

[This article is prerelease documentation and is subject to change.]

claims.where: Why it matters; Autonomy & actions; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness autonomous agents run from events such as arriving email rather than requiring a chat prompt.
claims.quote: Autonomous agents run when an event occurs in a connected service. For example, an agent can respond when an item is created in SharePoint, an email arrives, or a scheduled time occurs.

claims.claim: The agent's instructions and tools determine what it does with trigger event details.
claims.quote: The trigger sends event details to the agent. Your agent's instructions and tools determine what the agent does with those details.

claims.claim: One shared agent becomes one running instance per recipient.
claims.quote: Searched: shared autonomous administrator instances; shared autonomous agent owner disabled. Opened Share agents, Set up a shared autonomous agent, and Add triggers. These describe individual activation and connections, not a one-instance-per-recipient architecture.
claims.fix: Replace 'One shared agent becomes one running instance per recipient' with 'Each recipient activates the shared agent and connects the services it requires using their own credentials'.

claims.claim: Using a recipient's own connections limits actions to the permissions of that recipient's account.
claims.quote: The action runs under the end-user's identity. If the user lacks permission for something, the agent is unable to do it on their behalf - by design.

claims.claim: Run-only sharing requires user-authenticated trigger and tool connections rather than maker credentials.
claims.quote: Before sharing, configure the agent's triggers and tools for user authentication.

claims.where: Security & identity; Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Maker updates can require recipients to connect services or consent to changes on the agent management page.
claims.quote: The agent owner can update the agent, which might require you to connect or consent to the updates.

claims.claim: No approval setting specific to run-only shared autonomous agents is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: shared autonomous approval; Copilot Studio shared autonomous agents approval administrator instances reporting credits rates data policy running. Opened Share agents, Set up a shared autonomous agent, and Add triggers; no run-only approval setting was documented.

claims.claim: Recipients need to bookmark the management URL for health checks, repairs and update consent.
claims.quote: End users need to bookmark the agent management URL to check their agent's health, fix the agent, consent to maker updates to the agent, and other management tasks.

claims.claim: The management page's Enabled toggle pauses and resumes a trigger.
claims.quote: To pause a trigger without removing its configuration, turn the **Enabled** toggle off. Turn it on again when you want the trigger to run.

claims.claim: The management page has an Activity tab for reviewing recent and failed runs.
claims.quote: Use the **Activity** tab to review recent runs and identify failed runs.

claims.claim: The end-user management article does not document administrator visibility into individual recipients' instances.
claims.quote: Searched: shared autonomous administrator instances. Opened Set up a shared autonomous agent and Share agents; they document recipient setup, activity and maker sharing, not administrative listing or removal of recipient instances.

claims.where: summary; licensing.notes; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Each end user's autonomous usage is totalled and billed in Copilot Credits through the agent's hosting environment.
claims.quote: Each end user's autonomous agent usage is totaled and billed through the underlying environment where the agent is hosted.

claims.claim: For the Microsoft Copilot harness, Copilot Credits cover LLM tokens, tools and the harness itself.
claims.quote: For experiences powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness, Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself.

claims.claim: Administrators manage Copilot Credits in the Power Platform admin center and can allocate them to environments.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are managed through the Power Platform admin center. Administrators can allocate credits to environments and monitor usage to ensure that sufficient credits are available.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; controls[6].note; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The sharing prerequisites require recipients to have a Microsoft Copilot Studio per-user licence.
claims.quote: Users you share with have a Microsoft Copilot Studio per-user license.

claims.claim: The sharing prerequisites say users without a licence can sign up for a trial.
claims.quote: Users who don't have a license can sign up for a trial.

claims.claim: The mixed licensing model reflects a per-user prerequisite alongside consumption billing.
claims.quote: Users you share with have a Microsoft Copilot Studio per-user license. ... Each end user's autonomous agent usage is totaled and billed through the underlying environment where the agent is hosted.

claims.claim: The cost rating is variable because usage is metered in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Usage is billed based on consumption and measured in Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: User-opt-in describes the maker sharing and recipient activation needed to use this capability.
claims.quote: Recipients can use the *can use* link to activate the agent for themselves, connect the agent with their own credentials, and manage their permitted trigger settings.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; controls[0].api; summary; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: No dedicated tenant or environment admin switch or API for Can use autonomous-agent sharing is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio autonomous agent Can use admin disable sharing tenant environment policy; Can use sharing API PowerShell. Opened Share agents, Control how agents are shared, Limit sharing and both credential-control articles; no dedicated switch found.

claims.claim: The sharing prerequisites require Authenticate with Microsoft user authentication.
claims.quote: User authentication for the agent is configured to **Authenticate with Microsoft**.

claims.claim: The printed Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironmentGovernanceConfiguration call, including its parenthesised extendedSettings text, is the sharing-limits command.
claims.quote: Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironmentGovernanceConfiguration -EnvironmentName <EnvironmentId> -UpdatedGovernanceConfiguration $governanceConfiguration
claims.fix: Remove '(extendedSettings bot-limitSharingMode, bot-maxLimitUserSharing)' from the executable call. Put those property names in the note, with instructions to retrieve governanceConfiguration and set the extendedSettings values before invoking the documented command; use the cited agent-sharing example.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; controls[1].note; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Managed Environments sharing rules are configured at Manage > Environments > environment > Edit Managed Environments > Manage sharing.
claims.quote:
On the **Environments** page, select a managed environment.
5. In the command bar, **Edit Managed Environments**.
6. The sharing rules are located in the **Manage sharing** section.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Why it matters; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Managed Environments documents Editor and Viewer sharing controls but does not explicitly confirm their applicability to Can use run-only sharing.
claims.quote: Searched: Can use sharing limits Copilot; Copilot Studio autonomous agent Can use admin disable sharing tenant environment policy. Opened Limit sharing and Control how agents are shared; their permission rules name Editor and Viewer, not autonomous Can use.

claims.claim: The data-policy creation path is Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy > Assign connectors.
claims.quote: Select **Next**. The **Add an environment** page appears. ... Select **Next**. The **Assign connectors** page appears.
claims.fix: Include the omitted scope-selection step: Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy > Add an environment > environment > Add to policy > Assign connectors. Explain Next transitions and enter a policy name in the accompanying note.

claims.claim: New-DlpPolicy with only DisplayName and EnvironmentType is the automation equivalent for preventing event triggers by blocking the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector.
claims.quote: The New-DlpPolicy cmdlet creates a new DLP policy for the logged in admin's tenant.
claims.fix: Do not present policy creation alone as a connector-blocking command. Move this cmdlet to a clearly labelled generic policy-creation explanation, remove the module annotation from executable code, and keep the documented UI procedure for blocking Microsoft Copilot Studio; the displayed call contains no connector classification.

claims.claim: Configuring these data policies requires tenant admin or Environment Admin.
claims.quote: Be a tenant admin or have the **Environment Admin** role.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocking the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector in a data policy prevents makers adding event triggers.
claims.quote: To prevent agent makers from adding event triggers to their agents or running automated evaluations by using an authenticated account, configure a data policy that blocks the **Microsoft Copilot Studio** connector.

claims.claim: An enforced event-trigger data policy shows a detailed error in the Triggers section.
claims.quote: If the policy is enforced, a detailed error message appears in the **Triggers** section on the **Overview** page.

claims.where: Data exposure; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The cited data-policy guidance does not explain the precise treatment of already-running shared autonomous instances.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio data policy already running autonomous. Opened Configure data policies for agents; read Troubleshoot data policy enforcement excerpts. They describe real-time violations and publishing restrictions, not the lifecycle of already-running run-only instances.

claims.where: controls[3].ui; Governance controls table and following prose
claims.claim: The environment path given for Control maker credential options is sufficient to configure the control for hosting environments.
claims.quote: You can't configure this feature on the individual details page for environments that are in a group, you must use the group's details page.
claims.fix: Qualify the existing path as for ungrouped environments only. Add Manage > Environment groups > group > Settings > Product > Features > Copilot Studio agents > Control maker credential options for grouped environments, requiring a tenant admin with group access. State that group membership makes the environment options unavailable.

claims.claim: No API or PowerShell equivalent for Control maker credential options is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio Control maker credential options PowerShell API. Opened Control maker-provided credentials for authentication; search also returned connector-consent bypass, which governs a different setting. No equivalent credential-options command found.

claims.claim: Learn warns that preventing maker-provided credentials makes scheduled or autonomous background agents fail for missing credentials.
claims.quote: As a result, agents triggered by scheduled or autonomous events, or that attempt to run in the background, fail due to missing credentials. All agent triggers must involve an active user.

claims.claim: The maker credential policy changes tools for all agents in the affected environment or environment group.
claims.quote: All tools for all agents in the impacted environments instantly change to require end-user credentials at runtime.

claims.claim: Editing rights are separate from run-only sharing and can be assigned through environment security roles.
claims.quote: Add users to the agent's environment, and then assign users editing rights through the environment's security roles.

claims.claim: Embedded-maker-credential sharing is configured at Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Features > Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials.
claims.quote:
Go to **Manage** > **Environments**, and then select the environment that you want to configure.
3. Select **Settings**, and then select **Features**.
4. Find **Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials**.
claims.fix: Keep the cited path but report the differing Power Platform documentation at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/security/control-sharing-agents-with-embedded-maker-credentials: it marks the control preview and gives Security > Threat detection > Sharing agent with embedded maker credentials, then Environments or Environment groups > selection > Set up, with different mode labels.

claims.claim: No API or PowerShell equivalent for the embedded-maker-credential sharing setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials PowerShell API. Opened Configure sharing agents with embedded maker credentials and Control how agents are shared; read Power Platform control-setting excerpts. They provide UI configuration, not an automation equivalent.

claims.claim: The embedded-maker-credential control governs sharing and publishing, not an agent already running.
claims.quote: The sharing agents with embedded maker credentials control governs sharing and publishing. It doesn’t block an agent while the agent is running.

claims.claim: Embedded-maker-credential sharing enforcement does not retroactively unshare or disable existing agents.
claims.quote: Enabling enforcement doesn’t retroactively unshare or disable agents that were previously shared.

claims.claim: The documentation does not explicitly name Can use run-only sharing as an evaluation point for embedded-maker-credential enforcement.
claims.quote: Searched: Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials PowerShell API; Copilot Studio autonomous agent Can use admin disable sharing tenant environment policy. Opened Configure sharing agents with embedded maker credentials and Control how agents are shared; no explicit Can use statement.
claims.fix: Retain the narrow uncertainty about Can use but add the documented class-level qualification: connections configured for end-user credentials are not subject to this connection-sharing restriction. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-sharing-controls-limits#control-sharing-of-agents-that-use-maker-provided-credentials.

claims.claim: Resource-based spending policies are added at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > Add spending policy.
claims.quote:
In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to **Copilot > Cost Management**.
2. Select **Configuration**, and then select **Add spending policy**.

claims.claim: No automation equivalent for resource-based agent or environment spending policies is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot resource-based spending policy API PowerShell. Opened Manage Copilot Studio costs and Create spendingPolicy. The Graph create reference supports allUsersSpendingPolicy and selectedGroupsSpendingPolicy, not resource-scoped policies.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout; controls[5]
claims.claim: A resource-based spending policy can cover selected agents or environments and set a monthly spending limit.
claims.quote: Choose No limit or set a monthly spending limit for the policy.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Resource-based spending policies can also set an optional per-agent limit.
claims.quote: You can also set a per-agent limit so that no single agent covered by the policy uses more than the amount you specify.

claims.where: controls[5].note; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: A Microsoft 365 resource-based policy replaces covered Power Platform capacity allocations and billing plans, while existing configuration remains effective until opt-in.
claims.quote: Until then, your existing Power Platform admin center configuration remains in effect. ... Copilot Credit management moves to the Microsoft 365 admin center, replacing their Power Platform admin center capacity allocations and linked billing plans.

claims.where: controls[5].note; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Resource-based Microsoft 365 spending policies exclude AI Builder features and credits, and Microsoft warns against moving resources that use AI Builder.
claims.quote: Resource-based policies created in the Microsoft 365 admin center don't apply to AI Builder features or the credits they consume. ... Don't move resources, agents, workflows or environments that use AI Builder to these policies.

claims.claim: Learn recommends AI Administrator for Power Platform or Dynamics 365 administrators managing spending policies.
claims.quote: | Power Platform Administrator or Dynamics 365 Administrator | AI Administrator | Manage spending policies. |

claims.claim: No documented API or PowerShell equivalent for granting autonomous Can use sharing was found.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio autonomous Can use sharing API PowerShell. Opened Share agents and Control how agents are shared; results document the Share panel, not an API for this run-only permission.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: The cited pages do not publish a specific credit rate for autonomous run-only sharing.
claims.quote: Searched: autonomous run-only credits rates reporting. Opened Share agents and Overview of usage-based billing; read Billing rates and management excerpts, which explicitly concern the standard harness. No specific run-only rate found.

claims.claim: The cited pages do not describe how per-user totals for shared autonomous agents appear in admin reports.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot harness per-user consumption reports autonomous; autonomous run-only credits rates reporting. Opened sharing and billing pages; read Microsoft Copilot harness cost-management excerpts. They describe environment and agent reporting, not run-only per-user totals.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: The feature's sharing and management documentation does not say what happens to recipient instances when the maker is disabled.
claims.quote: Searched: shared autonomous agent owner disabled. Opened Share agents and Set up a shared autonomous agent; neither describes recipient execution after maker-account disablement. Results for Agent Builder and Dataverse ownership concern other mechanisms.

claims.where: rationale: risk versus controls[1].note and Governance controls
claims.claim: The risk rationale states that existing sharing controls do not cover Can use, while the body says applicability is unconfirmed.
claims.quote: Microsoft has not confirmed it applies to Can use sharing. ... the existing controls cover Editor and Viewer sharing, not Can use.
claims.fix: Replace the definitive exclusion in the risk rationale with 'Learn describes existing sharing limits in terms of Editor and Viewer permissions and does not explicitly confirm their applicability to Can use'. Keep the high risk judgement if desired.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout versus Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist tells administrators to check consumption by environment and agent, but the controls table has no consumption-monitoring row.
claims.quote: Check Copilot Credit consumption by environment and agent against the maker's estimate.
claims.fix: Add a consumption-monitoring row and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/billing-credit-overview: Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Copilot Studio for environment or tenant consumption, and the agent's Monitor page in Copilot Studio for agent totals.
